title: Signature Search-Leakage Ledger
description: Signature edition: every encrypted-search deployment records its exact leakage profile — what the server learns (access patterns, equality, order) — reviewed and signed off. Leakage is never implicit; the ledger makes it a reviewed decision, revisited when the threat model changes. This is a Signature original method.
method: Document the leakage profile per deployment; review against the threat model; sign off; revisit on change.
usage: Write the leakage profile before deploying; get signoff; revisit annually.

demo.code:
print('leakage profile: access pattern + equality (documented)')
print('threat model review: ACCEPTED (signed 2026-10-21)')

title: Signature Tokenized encrypted search
description: Signature edition: The practical middle ground: tokenize documents, encrypt tokens deterministically, and build a searchable encrypted index. Queries encrypt the same way and match index entries — fast like plaintext search, with deterministic-encryption leakage (equality patterns) as the stated tradeoff.
method: Tokenize; deterministic-encrypt tokens; build the index; query by encrypted token; accept and document equality leakage.
usage: Use for production encrypted search; document the leakage; pad frequent tokens.

demo.code:
print('index: enc("invoice") -> [d1,d9]; enc("urgent") -> [d3]')
print('search enc("urgent") -> [d3] (server sees token equality only)')

title: Signature Verifiable encrypted search
description: Signature edition: A malicious server could return wrong results; verifiable SSE adds proofs — the client checks completeness and correctness of results cryptographically. The server proves it searched the whole index honestly, or the client detects the lie.
method: Index with authentication (Merkle/hashes); server returns results + proof; client verifies before trusting.
usage: Use when the server isn't trusted for correctness; verification is cheap relative to search.

demo.code:
print('server returns 3 docs + Merkle proof of completeness')
print('client verifies: all matches returned, none omitted -> TRUSTED')

title: Signature Multi-keyword ranked encrypted search
description: Signature edition: Real search ranks: multi-keyword encrypted search computes relevance (TF-IDF style) over encrypted term frequencies using homomorphic addition or secure two-party ranking. Results come back ranked without the server seeing terms, frequencies, or the ranking computation's inputs.
method: Encrypt term frequencies; homomorphically accumulate scores; return top-k encrypted; client decrypts and verifies.
usage: Use for document search at scale; the homomorphic scoring is the cost center — optimize it.

demo.code:
print('query 3 keywords over 100k encrypted docs')
print('homomorphic scoring -> top-10 returned, ranked (server saw nothing)')

title: Signature Encrypted regex matching
description: Signature edition: Regular expressions over encrypted text via homomorphic automata evaluation: the regex compiles to an automaton, the server evaluates it homomorphically over encrypted characters. Log analysis and DLP on encrypted data — patterns matched, content unseen.
method: Compile regex to automaton; evaluate homomorphically per character; aggregate acceptance; client decrypts the verdict.
usage: Use for pattern scanning on encrypted logs; keep regexes small (automata cost).

demo.code:
print('regex: credit-card pattern over encrypted logs (FHE automaton)')
print('server: match at line 8812 (content unseen) -> alert with proof')

title: Signature Performance engineering for encrypted search
description: Signature edition: Encrypted search is 10-1000x slower than plaintext; engineering closes the gap: index sharding, GPU/FPGA acceleration of homomorphic ops, hybrid plaintext-metadata indexes, and caching frequent queries. Performance is what separates research prototypes from deployed systems.
method: Shard indexes; accelerate crypto ops; hybridize where leakage allows; cache; measure relentlessly.
usage: Benchmark on your data; hybridize deliberately (document each leakage); cache aggressively.

demo.code:
print('baseline FHE search: 40s/query -> sharded + GPU: 1.2s')
print('hybrid metadata index: 80ms (leakage documented, accepted)')

title: Signature Order-revealing search indexes
description: Signature edition: Range queries on encrypted text (dates, versions) use order-revealing or order-preserving encryption in the index: the server compares ciphertexts to answer ranges without decrypting. The leakage (order) is modeled and accepted for the columns that need it.
method: Index with ORE/OPE; range queries compare ciphertext; document order leakage per column.
usage: Use only for range-needed columns; model what order reveals about your data.

demo.code:
print('range [2026-01-01, 2026-06-01] on encrypted dates')
print('server compares ciphertext order -> returns matches (order leaked, accepted)')

title: Signature Private pattern matching (Yao-style)
description: Signature edition: Two-party private pattern matching: the pattern owner and text owner jointly compute matches via garbled circuits or OT, learning only the match positions. Neither reveals their input — the genomics and intrusion-detection use case (private DNA search, private signature matching).
method: Garbled-circuit pattern matcher (or OT-based); inputs stay private; output = match positions only.
usage: Use when both pattern and text are sensitive; the circuit cost scales with text length.

demo.code:
print('hospital pattern vs patient genome (both private)')
print('protocol: matches at positions [1042, 88123]; nothing else revealed')

title: Signature Wildcard and fuzzy encrypted search
description: Signature edition: Exact tokens aren't enough: wildcard and fuzzy search over encrypted data uses n-gram tokenization (encrypted n-grams match approximately) or homomorphic edit-distance circuits. 'Jon' finds 'John' without decrypting the directory — approximate matching under encryption.
method: Index encrypted n-grams; query expands to n-grams; rank by overlap; or compute homomorphic edit distance for precision.
usage: Use n-grams for interactive fuzzy search; reserve homomorphic edit distance for verification.

demo.code:
print('query "jon": n-grams {jo,on} match enc("john") n-grams {jo,oh,hn}')
print('ranked: John (0.67 overlap) -> returned')
